messages:
sasha: Quick follow-up from the auth surface RFC meeting. We need a pragmatic plan to reduce the number of accepted credential styles without breaking operator flows. Goal: single-parse path, preserve audit context, and make migration low-friction. cc @aj @maria @tim

aj: Sounds good. Do we have a preferred header shape? The gateway should be able to route without heavy parsing.

sasha: Sketch: introduce a single canonical header: `X-Redwood-Auth: kind=<kind>;token=<token>;hint=<hint>` where kind in {api_key, ephemeral, svc_token}. The hint is optional and only for routing/visibility (not authority). This lets us avoid touching Authorization for legacy consumers.

maria: I like explicit kind. Important: we MUST NOT trust client-provided scope/hint for RBAC. Always resolve token -> actor -> roles via identity service. Hint helps routing but not policy.

sasha: Agreed. Runtime will translate header -> normalized claim bag: actor_id, token_type, origin, ttl. We'll include origin=(legacy|unified) so audits keep provenance.

tim: How long do we accept legacy Authorization header? Many infra repos are slow to rotate. We should do a staged deprecation window.

sasha: Proposal: Accept both for 120 days. During that time emit deprecation audit events and a console banner for keys older than 60 days. At 120d, disable legacy for new token minting; at 240d, reject legacy completely. Opt-outs possible for Dedicated/Private with support-approved extensions.

aj: That seems safe. Implementation note: gateway will parse unified header first, fall back to legacy Authorization. Make the parse cheap and cache token->claims mapping with a TTL to avoid hitting identity service on every request.

maria: Cache TTLs are a tradeoff: shorter TTL -> faster revocation, more load. Recommend default 3m, route-level override to 30s for sensitive routes (admin, billing). Documented in route config.

stash: (typo, ignore)

tim: Edge cases: proxies that strip or rewrite headers, webhooks with signature tied to raw header, and legacy clients that embed key in query params. We need migration helpers (sidecar snippets) and docs for webhook signing updates.

sasha: We'll ship an nginx snippet and a tiny shim lib to preserve/translate Authorization -> X-Redwood-Auth for common proxies. Also include examples for Lambda edge and Envoy.

aj: Testing: parsing unit tests, fuzz unknown header shapes, integration tests where token maps to different actor roles, private deploy KMS-backed key tests, and a migration-lint that flags services still sending Authorization.

maria: For RBAC mapping: ensure identity service records the original token type in audit events. Also ensure policy evaluation uses actor_id roles with no shortcuts. We'll add a circuit-breaker to fail closed if identity service unreachable unless token cached and fresh.

sasha: Good point. Fail-closed for sensitive routes; fail-open low-sensitivity with metric alerting. Define rollback if auth failures spike >0.5% over baseline for 10 minutes.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: Feature flag created: auth.unified_header_enabled (default off in prod).

aj: Rollout plan: 1) accept new header (no changes to defaults); 2) enable in staging canary for 7 days; 3) opt-in Dedicated/Private customers; 4) enable for selected low-traffic hosted routes; 5) enable deprecation telemetry and console banners; 6) flip enforcement after window. Each step gated by telemetry (auth failures, latency).

tim: Operator onboarding: provide a one-time exchange flow to mint short-lived bootstrap tokens and then exchange them into scoped operator api_keys. Use single-use nonces to avoid replay.

maria: Also require explicit TTL on ephemeral tokens and audit the exchange path. Add unit tests that ensure revoked tokens stop working within TTL bounds.

sasha: Owners: aj -> gateway parsing + canary, tim -> sidecar/shim + operator flow, maria -> authz tests + lint, sasha -> docs + console messaging. I'll write the rollout playbook and link it here.

infra-bot: reminder: ticket ENGSEC-1310 created with checklist and dashboards.

sasha: Thanks all. If no blockers I'll open a PR with the header parser and the migration docs tomorrow. :thumbsup:
